subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Should OpenClaw make status and sessions usage JSON a stable per-session attribution surface for cron and channel labels, and which fields/privacy defaults should be part of that contract?
rationale: The missing behavior is not a broken current contract; it creates new stable public JSON fields and privacy policy for cron/channel attribution, which automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define a narrow additive JSON contract
options.body: Add optional stable fields such as sessionKind, cronJobId/name, and channelTargetKind while omitting or hashing target ids unless a separate explicit flag is approved.

options.title: Defer to diagnostics plugins
options.body: Keep core JSON unchanged and steer dashboard users toward diagnostics-prometheus/diagnostics-otel, accepting that per-session cron/channel joins remain outside the official usage rows.

options.title: Fold into the status-label tracker
options.body: Treat this as part of the narrower CLI/TUI label issue, which risks mixing display cleanup with broader API/schema work.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow additive JSON contract
recommendation.body: Add optional stable fields such as sessionKind, cronJobId/name, and channelTargetKind while omitting or hashing target ids unless a separate explicit flag is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses stable status output, session metadata display, and product/API scope, and the strongest history signal for status surface ownership points to steipete.
